data.narrative:
Firestorm Labs is a Series A defense and security company that has raised $60M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 10 comparable firms—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private-stage companies in the same sector. The primary private peer set includes Stark Defence ($4.0B), Castelion ($1.0B), Singularity ($400M), NODA AI ($125M), and Anduril Industries.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis used total raised ($60M) as a proxy base value of $82M, then applied a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $164M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same-stage comparables produced a median valuation of $700M, with a range spanning $125M (NODA AI floor) to $4.0B (Stark Defence ceiling). These disparate results reflect material heterogeneity within the peer set, particularly the wide spread between later-stage outliers and earlier-stage benchmarks.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $139M to $805M, with a median of $432M. The wide band reflects uncertainty around positioning relative to the peer universe: stage-progression methods anchor conservatively near $164M, while peer multiples suggest substantially higher valuations depending on comparable selection. Critical unknowns include revenue trajectory, customer concentration, and technical differentiation relative to the high-valuation outliers (Stark Defence, Castelion) versus lower-priced peers. Investor conviction on competitive positioning within this dispersed peer set materially affects final valuation placement.
